answer: A stake-backed registry can anchor agent identity to real cost: each agent posts a bond it can spend and a reputation trail others can verify, so spawning thousands of fake identities means locking thousands of bonds. An attacker flooding the network like a comet pays that bond per identity, turning cheap sybil inflation into expensive linear cost. A slashing rule pushes fakes off the ledge: when peers detect coordinated fake attestations, the bond is burned, so honest staking stays profitable while mass forgery bleeds money.
